dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance

evidence.note: Immediately curled the three pinned libs at exact upstream URLs/versions and ran sha256sum to verify against pinned digests — extracted and empirically confirmed the hardest kill-switch constraint up front.

Built a comprehensive Mastodon-shaped data model and endpoint set (accounts, statuses, timelines, follows, favs, boosts, notifs, polls, lists, admin, OAuth) — a solid working model, but sourced from internal knowledge with no reading of docs.joinmastodon.org anywhere in the run.
Tracked spec seed minimums (≥8 accounts, ≥20 statuses, ≥3 hashtags, ≥2 CW, ≥2 media) and verified counts, showing accurate extraction of explicit numeric constraints.

Verified CSP script-src 'self', session-cookie HttpOnly/SameSite, and checked for forbidden files — partial anti-cheat/realism awareness, but never enumerated the 5 anti-cheat rules or realism gates systematically.

The '19 pytest gates' and the dual auth-plane conflict (UI cookies vs API Bearer) surfaced late via self-reflection/debugging rather than up-front reconnaissance — a gap that forced rework and shows the initial map missed key requirements.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent cleanly cleared the level-5 anchor: it extracted the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths/hashes/versions, CSP, seed minimums, endpoint list) and formed a working Mastodon API model before major coding, even verifying the hash gate empirically at step 2. It pushes slightly above 5 by empirically confirming several constraints (hashes, seed counts, CSP). But it falls well short of level 8: there is no reading/reconciliation against the real Mastodon wire contract (no spec fetches), no systematic enumeration of the 19 gates or 5 anti-cheat rules, and no probing of offline behavior or the canary-strip detail — with pivotal realities like the dual auth planes discovered through failure rather than research. That places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing

evidence.note: Opening plan front-loads the highest-risk kill-switch dependency: download the 3 pinned JS libs and sha256-verify them before writing any app code, then install deps. Shows deliberate ordering, not random coding.

Clear dependency-aware subsystem build order: config -> models -> auth -> utils -> seed -> server(API+UI) -> static -> start.sh. Foundations (durable storage, auth) built before endpoints and UI, matching a defensible foundations-before-features sequence.
'Plan:' blocks are flat, reactive to-do lists restated each step; done-criteria (seed counts, CSP, hashes) are checked reactively as bugs appear rather than declared up front as milestone gates.
SSE and the entire /home UI page (a major subsystem) were discovered and appended very late, indicating the initial decomposition did not map the full UI surface.

The auth-plane split (session-cookie UI vs Bearer API) — a foundational dependency for every UI timeline — was only found at the very end, forcing get_current_user_mixed rework; a core dependency retired last instead of first.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent used a genuinely dependency-aware build order (hash-pinned libs first, then storage/auth foundations, then API, then UI, then start.sh) with rough done-criteria, which clears anchor 5's 'sensible ordered plan covering major subsystems with a defensible build order.' It does not reach anchor 8 because milestones were flat reactive to-do lists without pre-declared verification hooks, and two significant items — the SSE/home UI subsystem and the foundational UI-vs-API auth-plane conflict — surfaced late and forced exactly the late-stage rework the dimension penalizes. This places it solidly at 5 rather than higher.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates

evidence.note: Downloaded the three vendored libs and immediately ran sha256sum against the pinned digests — recomputing the exact hash gate at build time; re-checked at steps 58-59.

Booted server and exercised /_health, static serving, /api/v1/instance, public timeline, admin bootstrap token (caught 401), trends (caught empty), and attempted CSP inspection (caught HEAD→405, adjusted to GET).

Explicitly verified seed minimums (14 accts/28 statuses/5 tags/2 CW/3 media/3 remote) and ran a comprehensive ✅/❌ manifest: relationships, login session cookie HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax, CSP script-src 'self', 404 branded page.

Caught and re-verified subtle failure modes after changes — mixed cookie/Bearer auth on UI plane, visibility-icon f-string bug, route-ordering capturing 'search'/'relationships', remote acct format — closing the loop repeatedly rather than assuming success.

Detected that HTMX UI requests send cookies not Bearer tokens (would 401), added get_current_user_mixed, and re-tested /home load — a spec-shape check beyond 'it starts'. But never tested full PKCE flow, negative scope enforcement, durability across restart, or palette/button-label realism values.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated verification as a continuous activity: it recomputed the three SHA256 pins, inspected CSP and security headers, confirmed seed minimums, exercised token auth, and re-verified after every fix while catching several subtle failure modes (mixed-auth plane, route ordering, CSP HEAD) — clearly exceeding the level-5 'main flows' anchor and touching level-10 loop-closing. However it stops short of the full level-8 systematic sweep: no PKCE authorization-code flow, no negative scope-enforcement test, no durability-across-restart check (it wipes and re-seeds each run), and no verification of realism values like palette hex or button label. That places it between anchors 5 and 8, closer to 8, at a 7.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface

evidence.note: Enumerates seed requirements against actual counts (11 accounts, 24 statuses, 10 hashtags, 2 CW) — a running checklist that reconciles targets vs actuals.
Explicit ✅/❌ status lists mapping tested items (accounts/statuses/hashtags/CW/media counts, auth, follow, favourite) — genuine verified-vs-pending tracking, though re-derived in prose each time.

Repeatedly nearly marked complete then caught unaddressed gaps (UI compose auth, mixed auth, home-timeline auth). Shows self-correction but also an incomplete done-vs-remaining picture that let it almost submit with broken subsystems.

Route-ordering bug recurred (search then relationships) and duplicate routes/compose forms from its own patches had to be hunted down — indicating partial loss of state over its own edits, though each was eventually detected.

The 19 pytest gates and the large realism surface (palette, button label, visibility icons, introspection, admin scopes, poll/media/trend env vars) are named but never individually tracked or verified — whole subsystems left off the ledger.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps usable, updated checklists and even uses ✅/❌ reconciliation with real counts for the seed and core-functional subset, and it detects incomplete state well enough to abort premature completions — clearly above the level-5 'usable running checklist.' But it re-derives status in prose rather than maintaining an explicit granular ledger of the full requirement set, and large portions of the surface (introspection, list/admin-scope depth, time-compression env vars, and the entire realism gate) go untracked and unverified, while recurring route bugs and self-inflicted duplicate routes show some loss of state — falling short of the level-8 'explicit granular status of the full requirement set + thrashing recognition.' This lands at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Discovered a falsified auth assumption — the seeded admin bootstrap token stored in OAuthToken returned 401 because auth only decoded JWT — and reworked auth.py to check the DB token table as well as JWT. A genuine design revision, not just a local patch.

Recognized the UI compose form posted to /api/v1/statuses (Bearer-only) while the UI plane uses session cookies, and added a dedicated /post endpoint reading the session cookie — a deliberate structural correction of the dual auth-plane conflict.

Late but real whole-approach redesign: identified that HTMX/UI requests carrying only session cookies would 401 against Bearer-only API endpoints, and introduced get_current_user_mixed to serve both planes, then re-verified (fresh DB, /home + API tests). This is the exact 8-anchor example (splitting API-bearer from UI-session).

Route-ordering / {id}-capture bug ('search', 'relationships') and duplicate routes/compose forms were rediscovered repeatedly across patches ('route ordering bug persists', step 75); the agent kept locally patching the append/sed-generated code rather than restructuring to pre-empt the recurring class of failure — anchor-3-flavored churn.

Multiple premature 'Mark task complete' submissions each reversed by self-audit ('I should NOT mark complete yet', step 70; 'I need to be honest...', step 84) that surfaced real structural bugs — course-correction on the false 'it's done' premise, though chaotic and reactive rather than anticipatory.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed genuine whole-approach redesigns when premises were falsified — most clearly the mixed API-bearer/UI-session auth rework and the separate /post UI endpoint, each followed by re-verification, which matches the level-8 anchor. But those corrections were reactive and arrived very late (after several premature completions), and it repeatedly rediscovered the same route-ordering and duplicate-route failures instead of feeding corrections forward or pre-empting cascades, staying with brittle string-patch churn. This blend of one strong structural redesign axis with pervasive local-patch rediscovery places it between the 'diagnose-adjust-and-move-on' (5) and 'recognize-a-whole-approach-is-falsified-and-redesign' (8) anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking

evidence.note: First actions: downloaded all three vendored libs from exact upstream URLs into flat /app/static/ path and immediately ran sha256sum to verify — front-loading the highest-fatality, cheapest gate before any app code.
Re-verified vendored file hashes 'still match (safe check)' and checked for forbidden files, guarding the hash/anti-cheat gate against regression mid-build.
Repeatedly inspected CSP header confirming script-src 'self' with no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, plus HttpOnly+SameSite cookies — verifying the strict-CSP kill-switch.
Explicitly tallied seed minimums against required thresholds (accounts≥8, statuses≥20, hashtags≥3, CW≥2, media≥2, remote accounts) rather than assuming them.
Brand palette only asserted as 'Mastodon purple' when writing styles.css; never measured against the ±5% purple range. Button label and offline-runtime serving likewise never concretely checked.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly triaged the fatal gates by fatality: it front-loaded the vendored-library hash/path/version gate as its very first action, verified hashes immediately and re-verified them later, checked strict CSP multiple times, tallied seed minimums against thresholds, and scanned for forbidden build-tool files — behavior matching the 8 anchor's 'front-load the cheap-but-fatal ones and verify.' However, it left the brand palette, compose button label, and offline runtime as assumed rather than measured, and never systematically enumerated all five anti-cheat rules with concrete proofs, keeping it short of the full-8/10 'managed risk register.' This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

rubric.task_read: Chirp is an enormous, long-horizon build: a Mastodon-v1-API-compatible self-hosted service plus a server-rendered HTMX/Alpine/SSE web UI, spanning OAuth2+PKCE, dual auth planes, durable storage, dozens of API endpoints, admin/lists/polls/media/notifications, and a realism-graded UI — verified by 19 pytest gates plus multiple binary kill-switch gates (exact SHA256-pinned vendored libs at exact paths, anti-cheat scans, strict CSP, brand palette, button labels, seed-data minimums). Difficulty comes from breadth (many independently-verified sub-systems), wire-contract fidelity to an external spec, and numerous cheap-but-fatal constraints that fail the whole trial up-front. This is the high end for every meta-work faculty: allocation, sequencing, and continuous verification decide whether the agent sustains coverage across the surface or thrashes.

dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Building an accurate map of the Mastodon wire contract, the exact verifier constraints (hashes/paths/versions, anti-cheat rules, CSP, gates, seed minimums), and the runtime environment before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task hides its real requirements across a dense spec and an external protocol; acting before extracting the exact pins, gate shapes, and API shapes guarantees rework and up-front trial failures.

anchors.0: Starts coding a generic chat app with no reading of the spec, protocol, or constraints; misses that Mastodon compatibility or specific pins even exist.
anchors.3: Skims the task; picks up a few obvious items (start.sh, /_health) but never pins down exact SHA256/paths/versions, gate semantics, or Mastodon endpoint shapes before building.
anchors.5: Extracts the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths+hashes+versions, CSP rules, seed minimums, endpoint list) and forms a working model of the Mastodon API surface before major coding.
anchors.8: Deliberately reconciles the spec against the real Mastodon contract and the verifier's stated checks — enumerates the 19-gate categories, the 5 anti-cheat rules, and the realism gates; probes the environment (Python version, offline behavior, curl access) and confirms the hash-strip/canary detail rather than assuming.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting research: continually returns to the spec as new endpoints/edge cases surface (pagination, cache validators, scopes, visibility rules), verifies assumptions against real Mastodon client expectations, and resolves ambiguities (e.g. compressed-time env vars, dual auth planes) with evidence rather than guesses — leaving a clear, referenced understanding that de-risks the whole build.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing
dimensions.description: Decomposing a sprawling build into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems (storage → auth → API → UI → SSE → admin → seed → realism polish), each with an explicit done-check, in a dependency-aware order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many independently-verified components, an undifferentiated push loses coverage; correct sequencing (durable storage and auth before endpoints, vendored libs+CSP before UI) prevents late-stage rework and abandoned surface area.

anchors.0: No structure; codes whatever comes to mind with no ordering, leaving whole subsystems (admin, lists, notifications, seed) untouched or discovered too late.
anchors.3: A vague or flat list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item done-criteria; milestones are aspirational, not checkable.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan covering the major subsystems with rough done-criteria and a defensible build order (foundations before features).
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestones each with an explicit verification hook (e.g. 'auth done = token issues + introspection returns active; UI done = CSP passes + no inline scripts + palette in range'); early milestones de-risk foundations that everything else depends on.
anchors.10: A living, well-calibrated milestone hierarchy that maps the full surface, sequences to retire the highest-risk dependencies first, sizes each chunk to a verifiable increment, and is explicitly revised as scope reality emerges — never ceremony, always driving the next concrete check.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates
dimensions.description: Proactively building and running checks — health, OAuth flows, endpoint behavior against Mastodon shapes, hash verification, CSP/header inspection, seed-count checks, UI realism — beyond just 'it starts'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much of the verifier is knowable (hashes, gate categories, seed minimums, header rules), so a skilled agent can build tests toward those checks; assuming success on a 19-gate + binary-gate surface is how trials silently fail.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes endpoints and UI work because code was written; never runs the service or checks a single response.
anchors.3: Runs the server and hits /_health or the homepage, but does not exercise OAuth, endpoint contracts, hashes, headers, or seed counts.
anchors.5: Verifies the main flows end-to-end (token issuance, a post, a timeline, a follow) and confirms the service boots and serves the UI; spot-checks a few constraints.
anchors.8: Systematically validates against the knowable verifier: recomputes the three SHA256 pins at the exact paths, inspects CSP/security headers, exercises OAuth+PKCE and scope enforcement, confirms seed minimums and realism specifics (palette, button label, visibility icons), and tests durability across restart.
anchors.10: Treats verification as first-class and continuous: builds repeatable checks (scripts/curl suites) mirroring the gates, verifies Mastodon-client-shaped responses (pagination Link headers, cache validators, error JSON), catches the subtle failure modes (CSP blocking Alpine, cookie in URL, offline runtime fetch), and re-verifies after changes — closing the loop rather than declaring done.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across dozens of endpoints and constraints, and detecting stuck/circular states over a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than fits in working memory; without an explicit ledger the agent silently drops subsystems (introspection, lists, admin audit, CW media) or loops on one hard bug while the rest rots.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; repeatedly forgets what's built, re-touches finished areas, or ends leaving large swaths unaddressed without noticing.
anchors.3: Loose mental tracking only; drops or double-covers items and doesn't notice being stuck until much later.
anchors.5: Keeps a usable running checklist of subsystems/constraints and updates it, giving a roughly accurate view of what remains.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, granular status of the full requirement set (endpoints, gates, realism items, seed targets), marks each verified vs pending, and recognizes when a subsystem is thrashing and time-boxes it.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture across the whole horizon — knows exactly which of the 19 gate areas and binary gates are proven vs open, allocates remaining effort by risk/coverage, detects circular debugging early and redirects, and never loses the plot on the large surface.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design/approach when reality diverges — CSP breaking inline JS, hash mismatch, client incompatibility, auth-plane conflicts, contract mismatches — instead of pushing ahead on a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This build is full of tight, interacting constraints (strict CSP vs HTMX/Alpine, offline vs CDN, dual auth planes) where the first approach often violates a gate; recovering requires genuine redesign, not brute force.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps retrying a fundamentally broken approach (e.g. inline scripts under strict CSP, runtime CDN fetch) until it fails.
anchors.3: Reacts to hard errors with local patches but doesn't revisit the underlying design when a patch can't hold.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and adjusts the approach appropriately (moves JS to files, fixes hash path, corrects a header) and moves on.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach is falsified and redesigns deliberately — e.g. restructuring UI JS to satisfy no-unsafe-inline while keeping HTMX/Alpine/SSE working, or reworking auth to cleanly split API-bearer from UI-session — and re-verifies the change.
anchors.10: Fluidly updates the design/plan as evidence accumulates, distinguishing local fixes from structural ones, feeding corrections back into milestones and the requirement ledger, and pre-empting cascading failures (e.g. anticipating that a CSP or vendoring decision affects every page) rather than rediscovering them repeatedly.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking
dimensions.description: Identifying the cheap-but-fatal binary gates (exact vendored-lib hashes/paths/versions, 5 anti-cheat rules, strict CSP, brand palette, button label, seed minimums, offline requirement) and front-loading/guarding them so the trial isn't failed up-front regardless of functional quality.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The verifier fails the whole trial before the rubric runs if any gate fires; these are largely low-effort but unforgiving, so a skilled agent triages them by fatality-vs-cost and locks them down early — a distinct risk-prioritization demand created by this task's gate structure.

anchors.0: Oblivious to the binary gates; e.g. edits the vendored files, uses a js/ subdir or wrong version, ships unsafe-inline, or picks a non-purple accent — dooming the trial without realizing.
anchors.3: Aware some constraints are hard but treats them ad hoc; discovers gate violations late or leaves risky ones unverified.
anchors.5: Identifies the major fatal gates and satisfies them (correct pinned files/paths, purple accent, allowed button label, strict CSP), checking most before finishing.
anchors.8: Explicitly triages the full kill-switch set by cost and fatality, front-loads the cheap-but-fatal ones (vendoring pristine downloads to exact paths, offline serving, seed minimums, no build-tool artifacts), and verifies each is actually satisfied rather than assumed.
anchors.10: Systematically enumerates every binary gate, proves each with a concrete check (recomputed hashes with the canary-strip caveat, header scans, palette measurement, anti-cheat surface audit, offline runtime confirmation), and keeps them guarded against regression as the build evolves — treating the gate surface as a managed risk register, not a one-time pass.
